name: Shebna the treasurer
charge: Hewing himself a sepulchre on high in the rock, as if Jerusalem were his to be buried in; a shame to his lord’s house
summary: Isaiah was sent to Shebna, the treasurer over the king’s house, to ask what right he had to cut himself a tomb high in the rock of Jerusalem, in a city the Lord had called to weeping and that had answered with feasting (Isaiah 22:12-16). The Lord would toss him like a ball into a wide country to die there, a shame to his master’s house, and give his robe, his authority and the key of the house of David to Eliakim the son of Hilkiah (Isaiah 22:17-22). The teaching reads Shebna as the rulers of Israel carried into captivity, and Eliakim as a figure of Christ.
offenseFull: The burden of the valley of vision is the burden of Jerusalem. When the Assyrian came, the city counted its breaches, gathered the waters of the lower pool, pulled down houses to strengthen the wall, and built a reservoir between the two walls, but did not look to the One who made it (Isaiah 22:9-11; 2 Chronicles 32:2-4). They did everything but return to the Lord. The Lord called for weeping, mourning and sackcloth, and they killed oxen and sheep and feasted, telling one another to eat and drink because tomorrow they would die; and the Lord of hosts declared that this iniquity would not be purged from them until they died (Isaiah 22:12-14). He would go back to His place until they acknowledged their offence (Hosea 5:15).

Into that city the Lord sent Isaiah to one man, Shebna, the treasurer who was over the house, to ask what he had there and whom he had there, that he had cut out a tomb for himself high up and carved a resting place for himself in the rock (Isaiah 22:15-16). This was an actual man. The teacher reads from a Bible dictionary that Shebna was Hezekiah’s steward and scribe who carved himself an elaborate rock tomb, and that an inscription on a tomb in the Siloam hillside is believed to be his. But Shebna also represents the leadership, and the word is double, for the rulers of that day and of ours. While the city stood under judgment, the man over the king’s house was preparing a monument to himself.
judgmentFull: The Lord would carry him off in a mighty captivity, roll him up and throw him like a ball into a wide country, and there he would die, and there the chariots of his glory would be the shame of his master’s house; he would be driven from his office and pulled down from his post (Isaiah 22:17-19). Being thrown into a large country is captivity: the rulers and the people with them enslaved, turned and tossed into a strange land. The teacher notes that the chariots of glory can be read as vessels, ships, the fleets of Solomon and Jehoshaphat, and at last the ships that carried Israel back into bondage (Deuteronomy 28:68). A carved tomb in Jerusalem could not keep him from dying in a foreign land.

In that day the Lord would call His servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, dress him in Shebna’s robe, bind on his sash, and put his authority into his hand; he would be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah, and the key of the house of David would be laid on his shoulder, so that the doors he opened no one could close, and the doors he closed no one could open (Isaiah 22:20-22). The teaching makes Eliakim, whose name it gives as God raises up, a figure of Christ: the government is on his shoulder (Isaiah 9:6-7), he is a father to both kingdoms reunited under Christ, and he holds the key of David (Revelation 3:7). That key opens the understanding of the scriptures, and when the Lord shuts that door on one who falls away, nobody can open it. Eliakim was to be fastened like a nail in a sure place and be a throne of glory to his father’s house (Isaiah 22:23), which the teaching sets beside Christ the chief cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20).

When Rabshakeh stood at the conduit of the upper pool, Eliakim was the one over the household and Shebna was the scribe (2 Kings 18:18). The office Shebna held was a trust over the king’s house, and when he used it for himself, the Lord gave it to another.

text.text: And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.
Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, even unto Shebna, which is over the house, and say,
What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?
Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.
He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord’s house.
And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.
And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
Ye have seen also the breaches of the city of David, that they are many: and ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool.
And ye have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses have ye broken down to fortify the wall.
Ye made also a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool: but ye have not looked unto the maker thereof, neither had respect unto him that fashioned it long ago.
And when Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib was come, and that he was purposed to fight against Jerusalem,
He took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains which were without the city: and they did help him.
So there was gathered much people together, who stopped all the fountains, and the brook that ran through the midst of the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?
And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.
I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, even unto Shebna, which is over the house, and say,
What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?
Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.
He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord’s house.
And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.

And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.
And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.

And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;
And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.
And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;
And when they had called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, which was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder.
Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, even unto Shebna, which is over the house, and say,
What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?
Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.
He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord’s house.
And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.
And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.
And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.

In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall the nail that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down, and fall; and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off: for the Lord hath spoken it.
Ye have seen also the breaches of the city of David, that they are many: and ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool.
And ye have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses have ye broken down to fortify the wall.
Ye made also a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool: but ye have not looked unto the maker thereof, neither had respect unto him that fashioned it long ago.
And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.
